{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_29625db57b90420f97f7f1b6","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# bead-forge (`bf`)\n2\t\n3\t![bead-forge hero](hero.png)\n4\t\n5\t**bead-forge** is a Rust CLI that replaces `br` (beads_rust) as the bead management tool for AI-supervised coding workflows. It is a drop-in replacement for `br` — every command, flag, and output format is identical — with one critical improvement: **concurrent claiming is correct**.\n6\t\n7\t---\n8\t\n9\t## The Problem It Solves\n10\t\n11\t`br` has a race condition at its core. Claiming a bead requires two separate operations:\n12\t\n13\t```\n14\tbr ready --json          # read candidates (snapshot)\n15\t  ↓  (race window)\n16\tbr update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <worker>\n17\t  ↓  (race window)\n18\tbr show <id>             # verify the claim stuck\n19\t```\n20\t\n21\tWith 20 NEEDLE workers running simultaneously, multiple workers read the same candidate list, all select the same top bead, and all issue `br update`. SQLite last-writer-wins — 19 workers hold phantom claims on beads they don't actually own.\n22\t\n23\t`bf` eliminates this with a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` SQLite transaction:\n24\t\n25\t```\n26\tbf claim --assignee worker-7 --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --json\n27\t```\n28\t\n29\tThe entire read-score-update sequence runs inside one write lock. No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\n30\t\n31\t---\n32\t\n33\t## Architecture\n34\t\n35\t```\n36\tSQLite (live store)                    issues.jsonl (git artifact)\n37\t    │                                        │\n38\t    │  all reads and writes                  │  exported by bf sync --flush\n39\t    │                                        │  imported by bf sync --import\n40\t    ▼                                        ▼\n41\t  beads.db                            .beads/issues.jsonl\n42\t  (gitignored)                        (committed to git)\n43\t```\n44\t\n45\t**SQLite is the live database.** JSONL is a derived snapshot committed to git for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. `beads.db` is rebuilt at any time with `bf doctor --repair`.\n46\t\n47\t**No daemon. No server. No flock.** Each `bf` invocation is self-contained: open DB, acquire write lock, execute, release, exit. SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent reads during writes.\n48\t\n49\t---\n50\t\n51\t## Key Features\n52\t\n53\t### Atomic Concurrent Claiming\n54\t\n55\t```\n56\tWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT + score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\n57\tWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked until Worker 1 commits) → SELECT → ...\n58\t...\n59\tWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT\n60\t```\n61\t\n62\tThe entire claim pipeline — stale reclamation, candidate scoring, winner selection, status update, event recording — runs in a single SQLite write transaction. Guaranteed correct under any concurrency level.\n63\t\n64\t### Critical Path Scoring\n65\t\n66\t`bf` computes the **float** of each bead: how many hops it can slip before delaying its epic. Beads on the critical path (`float == 0`) receive a 1000-point bonus in the claim scorer, ensuring the fleet works on the most impactful beads automatically — without human priority curation.\n67\t\n68\t```\n69\t$ bf critical-path bf-epic-123\n70\t\n71\t  float=0  [bf-a3f8] Implement auth token refresh        in_progress\n72\t  float=0  [bf-b2c1] Fix concurrent session state bug    open\n73\t  float=2  [bf-d5e3] Update API documentation            open\n74\t```\n75\t\n76\t### Velocity-Aware Scoring\n77\t\n78\tWorkers declare their composition when claiming:\n79\t\n80\t```bash\n81\tbf claim --assignee worker-7 \\\n82\t         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\n83\t         --harness needle \\\n84\t         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\n85\t         --json\n86\t```\n87\t\n88\t`bf` tracks close times per `(model, harness, issue_type)` in `velocity_stats`. The claim scorer weights candidates by `impact / expected_duration` — the fleet maximizes throughput per unit time, not just raw priority. After 10+ completions per cohort, routing becomes measurably smarter.\n89\t\n90\t```\n91\t$ bf velocity\n92\t\n93\tModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\n94\tclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\n95\tclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\n96\tclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\n97\t```\n98\t\n99\t### Atomic Batch Operations\n100\t\n101\tReplaces NEEDLE's crash-unsafe create+dep chains. All operations execute in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. A crash mid-batch leaves zero partial state — SQLite rolls back automatically.\n102\t\n103\t#### Batch Operation JSON Schema\n104\t\n105\tBatch operations are specified as a JSON array of operation objects. Each operation must have an `op` field that specifies the operation type, followed by type-specific fields.\n106\t\n107\t**Operation types:**\n108\t\n109\t| Operation | `op` value | Description |\n110\t|-----------|------------|-------------|\n111\t| Create bead | `create` | Create a new bead with specified properties |\n112\t| Update bead | `update` | Modify fields of an existing bead |\n113\t| Close bead | `close` | Close a bead with optional reason |\n114\t| Add dependency | `dep_add_blocker` | Create a blocking dependency (A blocks B) |\n115\t| Remove dependency | `dep_remove` | Remove a dependency between beads |\n116\t| Add labels | `label_add` | Add labels to a bead |\n117\t| Remove labels | `label_remove` | Remove labels from a bead |\n118\t| Add comment | `comment` | Add a comment to a bead |\n119\t\n120\t**Placeholder references**: `@0`, `@1`, etc. resolve to the IDs of beads created at that position in the batch. You don't need to know child IDs in advance — `bf` substitutes them automatically.\n121\t\n122\t#### Operation Schema Details\n123\t\n124\t##### 1. Create (`create`)\n125\t\n126\tCreates a new bead. Returns the generated bead ID in the batch result.\n127\t\n128\t**Required fields:**\n129\t- `op`: `\"create\"`\n130\t- `title`: `string` — Bead title\n131\t\n132\t**Optional fields:**\n133\t- `type`: `string` — Issue type (default: `\"task\"`)\n134\t- `priority`: `number` — Priority level 0-4 (default: `2`)\n135\t- `description`: `string | null` — Bead description\n136\t- `assignee`: `string | null` — Assignee username\n137\t- `labels`: `string[]` — Labels to apply (default: `[]`)\n138\t\n139\t**Example:**\n140\t```json\n141\t{\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Implement auth\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 1, \"labels\": [\"urgent\"]}\n142\t```\n143\t\n144\t##### 2. Update (`update`)\n145\t\n146\tUpdates fields of an existing bead. Only specified fields are modified.\n147\t\n148\t**Required fields:**\n149\t- `op`: `\"update\"`\n150\t- `id`: `string` — Bead ID (can use placeholder like `@0`)\n151\t\n152\t**Optional fields:**\n153\t- `title`: `string | null` — New title\n154\t- `description`: `string | null` — New description\n155\t- `design`: `string | null` — Design document\n156\t- `acceptance_criteria`: `string | null` — Acceptance criteria\n157\t- `notes`: `string | null` — Notes\n158\t- `status`: `string` — New status (`open|in_progress|blocked|closed|...`)\n159\t- `priority`: `number` — New priority 0-4\n160\t- `assignee`: `string | null` — New assignee (empty string clears)\n161\t- `owner`: `string | null` — New owner\n162\t- `issue_type`: `string` — New issue type\n163\t\n164\t**Example:**\n165\t```json\n166\t{\"op\": \"update\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"status\": \"in_progress\", \"priority\": 0}\n167\t```\n168\t\n169\t##### 3. Close (`close`)\n170\t\n171\tCloses a bead. Idempotent — succeeds if already closed.\n172\t\n173\t**Required fields:**\n174\t- `op`: `\"close\"`\n175\t- `id`: `string` — Bead ID (can use placeholder like `@0`)\n176\t\n177\t**Optional fields:**\n178\t- `reason`: `string` — Close reason (default: `\"Completed\"`)\n179\t\n180\t**Example:**\n181\t```json\n182\t{\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"reason\": \"Fixed in PR #45\"}\n183\t```\n184\t\n185\t##### 4. Add Dependency (`dep_add_blocker`)\n186\t\n187\tCreates a blocking dependency: the blocker must close before the blocked bead can close. Validates against cycles and duplicates.\n188\t\n189\t**Required fields:**\n190\t- `op`: `\"dep_add_blocker\"`\n191\t- `id`: `string` — The bead being blocked (can use placeholder)\n192\t- `blocker`: `string` — The bead that blocks (can use placeholder)\n193\t\n194\t**Legacy aliases (deprecated but supported):**\n195\t- `parent` → `blocker` (the bead that blocks)\n196\t- `child` → `id` (the bead being blocked)\n197\t\n198\t**Direction:** Creates dependency: `id depends_on blocker` (blocker blocks id)\n199\t\n200\t**Example:**\n201\t```json\n202\t{\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"id\": \"bf-child\", \"blocker\": \"bf-parent\"}\n203\t```\n204\t\n205\t##### 5. Remove Dependency (`dep_remove`)\n206\t\n207\tRemoves a dependency between two beads.\n208\t\n209\t**Required fields:**\n210\t- `op`: `\"dep_remove\"`\n211\t- `id`: `string` — The bead that has the dependency\n212\t- `depends_on`: `string` — The bead to remove dependency from\n213\t\n214\t**Example:**\n215\t```json\n216\t{\"op\": \"dep_remove\", \"id\": \"bf-child\", \"depends_on\": \"bf-parent\"}\n217\t```\n218\t\n219\t##### 6. Add Labels (`label_add`)\n220\t\n221\tAdds labels to a bead. Duplicate labels are ignored (idempotent).\n222\t\n223\t**Required fields:**\n224\t- `op`: `\"label_add\"`\n225\t- `id`: `string` — Bead ID (can use placeholder)\n226\t- `labels`: `string[]` — Labels to add\n227\t\n228\t**Example:**\n229\t```json\n230\t{\"op\": \"label_add\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"labels\": [\"urgent\", \"backend\"]}\n231\t```\n232\t\n233\t##### 7. Remove Labels (`label_remove`)\n234\t\n235\tRemoves labels from a bead.\n236\t\n237\t**Required fields:**\n238\t- `op`: `\"label_remove\"`\n239\t- `id`: `string` — Bead ID (can use placeholder)\n240\t- `labels`: `string[]` — Labels to remove\n241\t\n242\t**Example:**\n243\t```json\n244\t{\"op\": \"label_remove\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"labels\": [\"deprecated\"]}\n245\t```\n246\t\n247\t##### 8. Add Comment (`comment`)\n248\t\n249\tAdds a comment to a bead.\n250\t\n251\t**Required fields:**\n252\t- `op`: `\"comment\"`\n253\t- `id`: `string` — Bead ID (can use placeholder)\n254\t- `text`: `string` — Comment text\n255\t\n256\t**Optional fields:**\n257\t- `author`: `string` — Comment author (default: `\"batch\"`)\n258\t\n259\t**Example:**\n260\t```json\n261\t{\"op\": \"comment\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"text\": \"Found edge case in login flow\", \"author\": \"worker-7\"}\n262\t```\n263\t\n264\t#### Batch Execution Examples\n265\t\n266\t**NEEDLE mitosis: split 1 bead into N children atomically**\n267\t\n268\tMethod 1: Dedicated mitosis command (recommended)\n269\t```bash\n270\tbf mitosis bf-a3f8 \\\n271\t  --children '[\n272\t    {\"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2},\n273\t    {\"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2}\n274\t  ]' \\\n275\t  --reason \"Split into children\"\n276\t```\n277\t\n278\tMethod 2: Direct batch with placeholder references\n279\t```bash\n280\tbf batch --json '[\n281\t  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n282\t  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n283\t  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"blocker\": \"@0\"},\n284\t  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"blocker\": \"@1\"},\n285\t  {\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"reason\": \"Split into children\"}\n286\t]'\n287\t```\n288\t\n289\t**Bulk status update:**\n290\t```bash\n291\tbf batch --json '[\n292\t  {\"op\": \"update\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"status\": \"in_progress\"},\n293\t  {\"op\": \"update\", \"id\": \"bf-456\", \"status\": \"in_progress\"},\n294\t  {\"op\": \"comment\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"text\": \"Started work\"}\n295\t]'\n296\t```\n297\t\n298\t**Label management:**\n299\t```bash\n300\tbf batch --json '[\n301\t  {\"op\": \"label_add\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"labels\": [\"urgent\", \"backend\"]},\n302\t  {\"op\": \"label_remove\", \"id\": \"bf-456\", \"labels\": [\"deprecated\"]}\n303\t]'\n304\t```\n305\t\n306\t#### Batch Response Format\n307\t\n308\tReturns a JSON array of results, one per operation:\n309\t\n310\t```json\n311\t[\n312\t  {\"op\": 0, \"status\": \"ok\", \"id\": \"bf-new1\", \"message\": \"Created bead bf-new1\"},\n313\t  {\"op\": 1, \"status\": \"ok\", \"id\": \"bf-new2\", \"message\": \"Created bead bf-new2\"},\n314\t  {\"op\": 2, \"status\": \"ok\", \"message\": \"ok: bf-parent blocked by bf-new1\"},\n315\t  {\"op\": 3, \"status\": \"ok\", \"message\": \"Closed bead bf-parent\"}\n316\t]\n317\t```\n318\t\n319\tOn error, the transaction rolls back and no partial state is committed:\n320\t\n321\t```json\n322\t[\n323\t  {\"op\": 0, \"status\": \"ok\", \"id\": \"bf-new1\", \"message\": \"Created bead bf-new1\"},\n324\t  {\"op\": 1, \"status\": \"error\", \"error\": \"Bead not found: bf-missing\", \"message\": null}\n325\t]\n326\t```\n327\t\n328\t#### Field Validation\n329\t\n330\tUnknown fields in any operation are rejected with a clear error message listing allowed fields. This catches typos early:\n331\t\n332\t```bash\n333\tbf batch --json '[{\"op\": \"create\", \"titlle\": \" typo\"}]'\n334\t# Error: Unknown field 'titlle' in operation 'create'. Allowed fields: op, title, type, priority, description, assignee, labels\n335\t```\n336\t\n337\t### Extensible Annotations\n338\t\n339\tArbitrary key-value metadata on any bead, transparent to `br`:\n340\t\n341\t```bash\n342\tbf annotate set bf-a3f8 needle_attempt 3\n343\tbf annotate set bf-a3f8 needle_session abc123\n344\tbf annotate set bf-a3f8 review_status needs_review\n345\tbf list --annotation needle_attempt=3\n346\t```\n347\t\n348\t### Operation History\n349\t\n350\t```bash\n351\tbf log bf-a3f8\n352\t\n353\t2026-04-29 10:00  CREATED     by: human                  \"Implement auth flow\"\n354\t2026-04-29 14:30  CLAIMED     by: worker-3 (sonnet-4-6)  open → in_progress\n355\t2026-04-29 15:45  COMMENT     by: worker-3               \"Found edge case\"\n356\t2026-04-29 16:00  CLOSED      by: worker-3               \"Completed\"\n357\t```\n358\t\n359\t---\n360\t\n361\t### Secret Scanning (Pre-Commit Hook)\n362\t\n363\t`bf` scans for secrets before writing to the database (see `.beads/config.yaml` → `secret_protection`). The `bf commit-check` command extends this to git — it runs as a pre-commit hook to block commits that would add secrets to `.beads/` files.\n364\t\n365\t```bash\n366\t# Manual scan\n367\tbf commit-check\n368\t# Exits 0 (clean) or 1 (secrets found) with detailed error output\n369\t```\n370\t\n371\t**Installation as git pre-commit hook:**\n372\t\n373\t```bash\n374\t# In your workspace repo\n375\tcat > .git/hooks/pre-commit << 'EOF'\n376\t#!/bin/sh\n377\tbf commit-check\n378\tEOF\n379\t\n380\tchmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit\n381\t```\n382\t\n383\t**What gets scanned:**\n384\t- `.beads/config.yaml` — workspace configuration\n385\t- `.beads/metadata.json` — database path settings\n386\t- `.beads/issues.jsonl` — bead data (git artifact)\n387\t\n388\t**Patterns detected:**\n389\t- AWS keys (`AKIA...`, secret access keys)\n390\t- GitHub tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`)\n391\t- Private keys (`BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`, `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`)\n392\t- JWT tokens\n393\t- API keys in URLs\n394\t- Database connection strings\n395\t- And more (same scanner as write-time protection)\n396\t\n397\t**Allowlist exceptions:**\n398\t\n399\tIf a pattern is legitimately non-secret, add to `.beads/config.yaml`:\n400\t\n401\t```yaml\n402\tsecret_protection:\n403\t  allowlist:\n404\t    - \"^AKIAEXAMPLE$\"  # exact string\n405\t    - \"password: test\"  # substring\n406\t```\n407\t\n408\t---\n409\t\n410\t## Commands\n411\t\n412\tMost commands accept `--format json|text|toon` for output and a global `-w/--workspace <path>` to target a workspace other than the current directory. The global `--no-auto-flush` flag disables the post-mutation incremental JSONL export for that one invocation (mutations stay db-only and marked dirty until `bf sync --flush-only`); see [Auto-Flush](#auto-flush-phase-71--the-checkpoint-tracks-the-live-store) below.\n413\t\n414\t```\n415\t# ── Lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n416\tbf create        --title \"...\" [--type <t>] [--priority <N>] [--description \"...\"]\n417\t                 [--assignee <a>] [--label <l> ...]\n418\tbf list          [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>]\n419\t                 [--annotation k=v] [--limit <N>] [--all] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\n420\tbf show          <id> [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\n421\tbf update        <id> [--title \"...\"] [--status <s>] [--priority <N>] [--assignee <a>]\n422\t                 [--description \"...\"] [--description-file <path>] [--acceptance-criteria \"...\"]\n423\t                 [--notes \"...\"] [--design \"...\"] [--due-at <RFC3339>]\n424\tbf close         <id> [--reason \"...\"]\n425\tbf reopen        <id>\n426\tbf delete        <id>\n427\tbf ready         [--limit <N>] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]   # unblocked beads\n428\tbf count         [--status <s>]\n429\t\n430\t# ── Claiming & concurrency ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n431\tbf claim         --assignee <id> [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--harness-version <v>]\n432\t                 [--any] [--fallback <mode>] [--workspace-paths <p> ...] [--dry-run]\n433\t                 [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\n434\tbf batch         [--file ops.json] [--json '[...]'] [--stdin]       # atomic multi-op\n435\tbf mitosis       <id> --children '[...]' [--reason \"...\"] [--format ...]   # split into children\n436\t\n437\t# ── Dependencies & structure ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n438\tbf dep add       <blocker> --blocks <blocked> [-t <type>]   # blocker must close first\n439\tbf dep remove    <issue> <depends-on>\n440\tbf dep list      <id>\n441\tbf dep tree      <id> [-d down|up|both] [--max-depth <N>] [--format ...] [--json]\n442\tbf critical-path <epic-id> [--max-depth <N>] [--format ...]\n443\t\n444\t# ── Labels, comments, annotations ────────────────────────────────────────────\n445\tbf label add     --label <l> [<l> ...] <id>\n446\tbf label remove  --label <l> [<l> ...] <id>\n447\tbf label list    [<id>]                  # all unique labels if id omitted\n448\tbf labels        <id> [--format text|json]                  # efficient single-bead SELECT\n449\tbf comments add  <id> <text ...>\n450\tbf comments list <id>\n451\tbf annotate set    <id> <key> <value>\n452\tbf annotate get    <id> <key>\n453\tbf annotate remove <id> <key>\n454\tbf annotate list   <id>\n455\tbf annotate clear  <id>\n456\t\n457\t# ── Query & history ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n458\tbf search        [<query>] [-s <status> ...] [-t <type> ...] [--assignee <a>]\n459\t                 [-l <label> ...] [--priority-min <N>] [--priority-max <N>] [--limit <N>]\n460\t                 [--format json|text|toon]\n461\tbf recent        [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>]\n462\t                 [--since <RFC3339>] [--before <RFC3339>] [-t <period>] [-n <N>]\n463\t                 [--format json|text|toon] [--json]           # period: e.g. 1h, 24h, 7d, 4w\n464\tbf log           [<id>] [--limit <N>] [--since <RFC3339>] [--actor <a>]\n465\t                 [--status-changes] [--diff] [--git] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\n466\tbf stats         [--by-type] [--by-priority] [--by-assignee] [--by-label] [--format ...]\n467\tbf velocity      [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--format json|text|toon]\n468\t\n469\t# ── Maintenance & config ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n470\tbf sync          [--flush-only] [--import-only]\n471\tbf merge-jsonl   --ours <A> --theirs <B> [--base <O>] [--output <path>]  # 3-way JSONL merge / git driver\n472\tbf doctor        [--repair [--flush-first] [--force]] [--reclaim-stale [--ttl <minutes>]]  # no flags = health check\n473\tbf rotate        [--days <N>] [--dry-run]\n474\tbf migrate       [--workspace <p>] [--from-jsonl] [--seed-velocity] [--dry-run] [--skip-verify]\n475\tbf init          [--prefix <p>]\n476\tbf schema        [<target|id>] [--format json|text]      # \"all\" = DDL; a bead id = full JSON\n477\tbf config        list | get <key> | set <key> <value> | path\n478\tbf commit-check  # git pre-commit hook for secret scanning\n479\t```\n480\t\n481\tAll `br` commands work identically. `bf` is a strict superset.\n482\t\n483\t---\n484\t\n485\t## Output Formats\n486\t\n487\tMost read commands accept `--format text|json|toon` (or the `--json` alias for\n488\t`--format json`). The JSON shape depends on **which command** you run, and it is\n489\tnot always a JSON array.\n490\t\n491\t### Listing commands emit JSONL — not a JSON array\n492\t\n493\t`bf list`, `bf ready`, `bf search`, and `bf recent` with `--format json` emit\n494\t**JSONL**: one self-contained, compact JSON object per line, joined by newlines,\n495\twith **no array wrapper** and no commas between objects.\n496\t\n497\t```bash\n498\t$ bf list --format json\n499\t{\"id\":\"test-3qv\",\"title\":\"alpha task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,\"issue_type\":\"task\",\"assignee\":null,\"labels\":[],\"created_at\":\"2026-07-22T15:54:16Z\",...}\n500\t{\"id\":\"test-2c4\",\"title\":\"beta task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,\"issue_type\":\"task\",\"assignee\":null,\"labels\":[],\"created_at\":\"2026-07-22T15:54:16Z\",...}\n501\t```\n502\t\n503\tThe concatenated stdout is **not** valid JSON (`{\"a\":1}\\n{\"b\":2}` is two values,\n504\tnot one), so you cannot `json.loads()` the whole buffer. Parse it **line by\n505\tline**:\n506\t\n507\t```python\n508\timport json, subprocess\n509\tout = subprocess.check_output([\"bf\", \"list\", \"--format\", \"json\"], text=True)\n510\tbeads = [json.loads(line) for line in out.splitlines() if line.strip()]\n511\t```\n512\t\n513\t```bash\n514\t# jq: slurp the JSONL lines into one array, then operate on it\n515\tbf list --format json | jq -s 'map(.id)'\n516\t```\n517\t\n518\tTwo keys are **always** present on every emitted object, even on a bare bead:\n519\t\n520\t- `assignee` — `null` when unassigned (never omitted)\n521\t- `labels` — an array, `[]` when empty (never omitted)\n522\t\n523\tThe on-disk `issues.jsonl` checkpoint (written by `bf sync`) omits these when\n524\tunset to stay compact; the CLI `--format json` path normalizes them back so a\n525\tdownstream struct with non-optional `assignee`/`labels` fields deserializes\n526\tcleanly.\n527\t\n528\t**Empty results differ by command:**\n529\t\n530\t| Command | Empty `--format json` output |\n531\t|---------|------------------------------|\n532\t| `bf list` | nothing (empty stdout) |\n533\t| `bf search` / `bf recent` | nothing (empty stdout) |\n534\t| `bf ready` | `[]` |\n535\t\n536\t`ready` is the one listing command that special-cases emptiness to `[]`; the\n537\tothers print nothing at all.\n538\t\n539\t### `bf show` emits a one-element array\n540\t\n541\tUnlike the listing commands, `bf show <id> --format json` wraps the single bead\n542\tin a **JSON array of one element**:\n543\t\n544\t```bash\n545\t$ bf show test-3qv --format json\n546\t[{\"id\":\"test-3qv\",\"title\":\"alpha task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,...}]\n547\t```\n548\t\n549\tThis is deliberate: NEEDLE's `parse_single_bead` expects `Vec<Bead>` and takes\n550\tthe first element, so `show` ships an array to stay parse-compatible with that\n551\tcode path.\n552\t\n553\t### `bf claim` emits a single object\n554\t\n555\t`bf claim --json` prints one JSON object describing the claim (or `{}` when\n556\tnothing was claimed) — never an array, never an `Issue`:\n557\t\n558\t```bash\n559\t$ bf claim --assignee worker-7 --json\n560\t{\"bead_id\":\"test-3qv\",\"assignee\":\"worker-7\",\"reclaimed\":0}\n561\t```\n562\t\n563\t`bf velocity --format json` emits a JSON array of stat objects (`[]` when empty).\n564\t\n565\t### `br` produces byte-identical output\n566\t\n567\t`br` delegates to the `bf` binary — either directly (a symlink, as installed by\n568\t`ln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br`) or via a logging shim that writes a\n569\tdeprecation-telemetry line and then `exec bf \"$@\"`. Neither path touches stdout,\n570\tso every `br` command emits **byte-identical** output to its `bf` equivalent —\n571\tsame JSONL, same array wrapping for `show`, same empty-case behavior. A parser\n572\twritten for `br list --format json` works unchanged for `bf list --format json`,\n573\tand vice versa.\n574\t\n575\t---\n576\t\n577\t## NEEDLE Integration\n578\t\n579\tReplace the five non-atomic `br` chains in `bead_store/mod.rs`:\n580\t\n581\t| Old (racy) | New (atomic) |\n582\t|-----------|--------------|\n583\t| `br ready` → `br update` → `br show` (3 calls, 2 race windows) | `bf claim` (1 call, 1 transaction) |\n584\t| `br create` + `br dep add` (orphan if crash between) | `bf batch` (crash-safe, all-or-nothing) |\n585\t| `br show` just to get `.labels` field | `bf labels <id>` (direct `SELECT` on labels table) |\n586\t| N × `br label add` loops (N processes) | `bf label <id> add l1 l2 l3` (one transaction) |\n587\t\n588\tBackward compatibility — install `br` as a symlink:\n589\t\n590\t```bash\n591\tln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n592\t```\n593\t\n594\t---\n595\t\n596\t## Compatibility\n597\t\n598\t`bf` reads and writes the same SQLite schema and JSONL format as `br`. A workspace used by `bf` can be read by `br` and vice versa. Verified by three test suites (see plan §Compatibility Verification):\n599\t\n600\t1. **JSONL round-trip**: `br list --format json` == `bf list --format json` on the same workspace\n601\t2. **SQLite compat**: `bf` writes, `br` reads, `br doctor` passes\n602\t3. **Claim race**: 20 concurrent `bf claim` processes, 10 beads — exactly 10 claims succeed, no bead claimed twice\n603\t\n604\t---\n605\t\n606\t## Reliability\n607\t\n608\t- **rusqlite** (standard SQLite C library) — not FrankenSQLite, which had known corruption under concurrent writes\n609\t- **WAL mode** — concurrent reads never block writes; writers queue, not corrupt\n610\t- **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — acquires write lock before any reads; eliminates TOCTOU\n611\t- **`SQLITE_BUSY` retry** — exponential backoff up to 5 retries; converts contention spikes to short waits\n612\t\n613\t### Data Authority Model\n614\t\n615\t**bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br**:\n616\t\n617\t| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n618\t|------|----------------|-----------------|\n619\t| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n620\t| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n621\t\n622\tThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. All mutations (create/update/claim) go to SQLite. With `sync.auto_flush` (default **on**), every successful mutation also incrementally exports the changed beads to `issues.jsonl`, so the checkpoint tracks the live store instead of trailing it — a separate flush is no longer needed in normal operation.\n623\t\n624\t### Auto-Flush (Phase 7.1) — the checkpoint tracks the live store\n625\t\n626\tWith `sync.auto_flush` (default **on**), every successful mutation (`create`/`update`/`claim`/`close`/`batch`) incrementally exports just the changed beads to `issues.jsonl` (a surgical line replacement, not a full rewrite). The JSONL artifact therefore stays current with SQLite after every command — no separate flush step is required in normal operation. Read-only and diagnostic commands never write the JSONL.\n627\t\n628\t```yaml\n629\t# .beads/config.yaml\n630\tsync:\n631\t  auto_flush: true     # default; set false to make mutations db-only until bf sync --flush-only\n632\t```\n633\t\n634\t```bash\n635\tbf create --title \"...\"               # auto-flushed by default → already in issues.jsonl\n636\tbf create --title \"...\" --no-auto-flush   # per-invocation override: db-only, marked dirty\n637\t```\n638\t\n639\t**Flush failure never fails the mutation.** Auto-flush is best-effort: if the incremental export fails, the mutation still commits, the dirty mark is retained, and the failure is surfaced loudly — a `warning:` line on stderr and a non-null `warning` field in the `--json` envelope naming the recovery command. The dirty bead stays recoverable.\n640\t\n641\t**Named recovery.** `bf sync --flush-only` is the explicit checkpoint and the recovery path: it clears the entire `dirty_issues` set and rewrites a **full** checkpoint (every bead, not just the dirty one). Run it after an auto-flush warning, or to produce a clean git-committable snapshot:\n642\t\n643\t```bash\n644\tbf sync --flush-only\n645\t```\n646\t\n647\t### Repair safety — protection is in the doctor, not a manual ritual\n648\t\n649\t`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from `issues.jsonl`. Because auto-flush keeps the checkpoint current, the old \"ALWAYS `bf sync --flush-only` before repair\" ritual (added after the 2026-06-10 incident where seven agents across seven workspaces each lost their first batch of fresh beads to a post-create `doctor --repair`; four db-only beads in ARMOR — bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44 — were permanently lost) is **obsolete**. The data-loss guard now lives in the doctor command itself: it **refuses** to repair when unflushed (db-only) beads exist, and tells you exactly what to do.\n650\t\n651\t```bash\n652\tbf doctor                              # health check — reports \"Unflushed beads: N\" if any\n653\tbf doctor --repair                     # REFUSES if unflushed beads exist (no data loss)\n654\tbf doctor --repair --flush-first       # checkpoint unflushed beads first, then rebuild\n655\tbf doctor --repair --force             # proceed anyway — unflushed beads WILL be lost\n656\t```\n657\t\n658\tKilling a worker at any point between mutation and flush loses nothing that `git diff .beads/` can't show: with auto-flush on the bead is already in the artifact when the command returns; with auto-flush off the bead survives in SQLite (marked dirty) and is recovered by `bf sync --flush-only`. Pinned by `tests/recovery_and_exit_criteria.rs`.\n659\t\n660\t### Multi-Box & Fleet Hardening (Phase 7.9)\n661\t\n662\tWhen the same repo is checked out on several boxes, each keeps its own live `beads.db` and shares state through the git-committed `issues.jsonl`. Three layers defend that shared artifact:\n663\t\n664\t**Three-way JSONL merge** — a plain git text merge of `issues.jsonl` is unsafe: each line is a whole bead, so a textual conflict marker corrupts JSON and \"take theirs\" silently drops beads. `bf merge-jsonl` merges **per-bead** against a common ancestor instead. Resolution is deterministic: a one-sided edit is taken as-is; a two-sided edit resolves last-writer-wins by `updated_at` (ties broken by content hash, so the result is independent of which box runs the merge); a delete that races a concurrent edit keeps the edit (never silently discards work). Wire it as a git merge driver:\n665\t\n666\t```bash\n667\tgit config merge.beads.name   \"bead-forge 3-way JSONL merge\"\n668\tgit config merge.beads.driver \"bf merge-jsonl --base %O --ours %A --theirs %B --output %A\"\n669\techo '.beads/issues.jsonl merge=beads' >> .gitattributes\n670\t```\n671\t\n672\t**Merge anchor** (`.beads/beads.base.jsonl`) — every full flush/import refreshes this snapshot of the last state this box agreed on with the artifact. It is the fallback three-way base for `bf merge-jsonl` when git does not supply `%O` (out-of-band merges across checkouts). Local-only; git-ignored.\n673\t\n674\t**Pre-export history backups** (`.beads/.bf_history/`) — before every full flush overwrites `issues.jsonl`, the previous version is copied into `.bf_history/` and pruned to the newest `history.max_backups` snapshots (default 20). One more recovery layer under a bad export or merge. Enabled by default; disable with `history.enabled: false` in `config.yaml`. Local-only; git-ignored.\n675\t\n676\t**Fleet concurrency tests** (`tests/fleet_concurrency.rs`) — spawn N concurrent `bf` *processes* doing create/claim/close and assert the upstream bug classes stay dead: no parallel-write silent loss (`count` equals successful creates), no loss across flush + fresh-DB reimport, and no bead claimed twice under a 20-worker herd on 15 beads.\n677\t\n678\t---\n679\t\n680\t## Implementation\n681\t\n682\tSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](plan/plan.md) for the complete implementation plan including:\n683\t\n684\t- Exact SQLite schema (all 13 tables + indexes)\n685\t- `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` retry wrapper implementation\n686\t- Critical path CTE algorithm\n687\t- Velocity stats schema and claim scoring formula\n688\t- Compatibility verification test suites\n689\t- NEEDLE integration specifics (file, line numbers, before/after)\n690\t\n691\t---\n692\t\n693\t## Migration from br to bf\n694\t\n695\t### Output Format Compatibility (no parser changes)\n696\t\n697\tMigrating to `bf` requires **no changes to JSON consumers**. `bf` is a drop-in\n698\treplacement: every command emits byte-identical output to `br`, because `br`\n699\tdelegates to the `bf` binary (via symlink, or a logging shim that `exec bf\n700\t\"$@\"`) and never alters stdout.\n701\t\n702\tThe format to keep in mind (full details in [§ Output Formats](#output-formats)):\n703\t\n704\t- `list` / `ready` / `search` / `recent --format json` → **JSONL** (one object\n705\t  per line, not a JSON array). It is a drop-in replacement for `br` — every command, flag, and output format is identical — with one critical improvement: **concurrent claiming is correct**.\n\n---\n\n## The Problem It Solves\n\n`br` has a race condition at its core. Claiming a bead requires two separate operations:\n\n```\nbr ready --json          # read candidates (snapshot)\n  ↓  (race window)\nbr update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <worker>\n  ↓  (race window)\nbr show <id>             # verify the claim stuck\n```\n\nWith 20 NEEDLE workers running simultaneously, multiple workers read the same candidate list, all select the same top bead, and all issue `br update`. SQLite last-writer-wins — 19 workers hold phantom claims on beads they don't actually own.\n\n`bf` eliminates this with a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` SQLite transaction:\n\n```\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --json\n```\n\nThe entire read-score-update sequence runs inside one write lock. No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\nSQLite (live store)                    issues.jsonl (git artifact)\n    │                                        │\n    │  all reads and writes                  │  exported by bf sync --flush\n    │                                        │  imported by bf sync --import\n    ▼                                        ▼\n  beads.db                            .beads/issues.jsonl\n  (gitignored)                        (committed to git)\n```\n\n**SQLite is the live database.** JSONL is a derived snapshot committed to git for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. `beads.db` is rebuilt at any time with `bf doctor --repair`.\n\n**No daemon. No server. No flock.** Each `bf` invocation is self-contained: open DB, acquire write lock, execute, release, exit. SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent reads during writes.\n\n---\n\n## Key Features\n\n### Atomic Concurrent Claiming\n\n```\nWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT + score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\nWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked until Worker 1 commits) → SELECT → ...\n...\nWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT\n```\n\nThe entire claim pipeline — stale reclamation, candidate scoring, winner selection, status update, event recording — runs in a single SQLite write transaction. Guaranteed correct under any concurrency level.\n\n### Critical Path Scoring\n\n`bf` computes the **float** of each bead: how many hops it can slip before delaying its epic. Beads on the critical path (`float == 0`) receive a 1000-point bonus in the claim scorer, ensuring the fleet works on the most impactful beads automatically — without human priority curation.\n\n```\n$ bf critical-path bf-epic-123\n\n  float=0  [bf-a3f8] Implement auth token refresh        in_progress\n  float=0  [bf-b2c1] Fix concurrent session state bug    open\n  float=2  [bf-d5e3] Update API documentation            open\n```\n\n### Velocity-Aware Scoring\n\nWorkers declare their composition when claiming:\n\n```bash\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 \\\n         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\n         --harness needle \\\n         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\n         --json\n```\n\n`bf` tracks close times per `(model, harness, issue_type)` in `velocity_stats`. The claim scorer weights candidates by `impact / expected_duration` — the fleet maximizes throughput per unit time, not just raw priority. After 10+ completions per cohort, routing becomes measurably smarter.\n\n```\n$ bf velocity\n\nModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\nclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\nclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\nclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\n```\n\n### Atomic Batch Operations\n\nReplaces NEEDLE's crash-unsafe create+dep chains. All operations execute in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. A crash mid-batch leaves zero partial state — SQLite rolls back automatically.\n\n#### Batch Operation JSON Schema\n\nBatch operations are specified as a JSON array of operation objects. Each operation must have an `op` field that specifies the operation type, followed by type-specific fields.\n\n**Operation types:**\n\n| Operation | `op` value | Description |\n|-----------|------------|-------------|\n| Create bead | `create` | Create a new bead with specified properties |\n| Update bead | `update` | Modify fields of an existing bead |\n| Close bead | `close` | Close a bead with optional reason |\n| Add dependency | `dep_add_blocker` | Create a blocking dependency (A blocks B) |\n| Remove dependency | `dep_remove` | Remove a dependency between beads |\n| Add labels | `label_add` | Add labels to a bead |\n| Remove labels | `label_remove` | Remove labels from a bead |\n| Add comment | `comment` | Add a comment to a bead |\n\n**Placeholder references**: `@0`, `@1`, etc. resolve to the IDs of beads created at that position in the batch. You don't need to know child IDs in advance — `bf` substitutes them automatically.\n\n#### Operation Schema Details\n\n##### 1. Create (`create`)\n\nCreates a new bead. Returns the generated bead ID in the batch result.\n\n**Required fields:**\n- `op`: `\"create\"`\n- `title`: `string` — Bead title\n\n**Optional fields:**\n- `type`: `string` — Issue type (default: `\"task\"`)\n- `priority`: `number` — Priority level 0-4 (default: `2`)\n- `description`: `string | null` — Bead description\n- `assignee`: `string | null` — Assignee username\n- `labels`: `string[]` — Labels to apply (default: `[]`)\n\n**Example:**\n```json\n{\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Implement auth\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 1, \"labels\": [\"urgent\"]}\n```\n\n##### 2. Update (`update`)\n\nUpdates fields of an existing bead. Only specified fields are modified.\n\n**Required fields:**\n- `op`: `\"update\"`\n- `id`: `string` — Bead ID (can use placeholder like `@0`)\n\n**Optional fields:**\n- `title`: `string | null` — New title\n- `description`: `string | null` — New description\n- `design`: `string | null` — Design document\n- `acceptance_criteria`: `string | null` — Acceptance criteria\n- `notes`: `string | null` — Notes\n- `status`: `string` — New status (`open|in_progress|blocked|closed|...`)\n- `priority`: `number` — New priority 0-4\n- `assignee`: `string | null` — New assignee (empty string clears)\n- `owner`: `string | null` — New owner\n- `issue_type`: `string` — New issue type\n\n**Example:**\n```json\n{\"op\": \"update\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"status\": \"in_progress\", \"priority\": 0}\n```\n\n##### 3. Close (`close`)\n\nCloses a bead. Idempotent — succeeds if already closed.\n\n**Required fields:**\n- `op`: `\"close\"`\n- `id`: `string` — Bead ID (can use placeholder like `@0`)\n\n**Optional fields:**\n- `reason`: `string` — Close reason (default: `\"Completed\"`)\n\n**Example:**\n```json\n{\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"reason\": \"Fixed in PR #45\"}\n```\n\n##### 4. Add Dependency (`dep_add_blocker`)\n\nCreates a blocking dependency: the blocker must close before the blocked bead can close. Validates against cycles and duplicates.\n\n**Required fields:**\n- `op`: `\"dep_add_blocker\"`\n- `id`: `string` — The bead being blocked (can use placeholder)\n- `blocker`: `string` — The bead that blocks (can use placeholder)\n\n**Legacy aliases (deprecated but supported):**\n- `parent` → `blocker` (the bead that blocks)\n- `child` → `id` (the bead being blocked)\n\n**Direction:** Creates dependency: `id depends_on blocker` (blocker blocks id)\n\n**Example:**\n```json\n{\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"id\": \"bf-child\", \"blocker\": \"bf-parent\"}\n```\n\n##### 5. Remove Dependency (`dep_remove`)\n\nRemoves a dependency between two beads.\n\n**Required fields:**\n- `op`: `\"dep_remove\"`\n- `id`: `string` — The bead that has the dependency\n- `depends_on`: `string` — The bead to remove dependency from\n\n**Example:**\n```json\n{\"op\": \"dep_remove\", \"id\": \"bf-child\", \"depends_on\": \"bf-parent\"}\n```\n\n##### 6. Add Labels (`label_add`)\n\nAdds labels to a bead. Duplicate labels are ignored (idempotent).\n\n**Required fields:**\n- `op`: `\"label_add\"`\n- `id`: `string` — Bead ID (can use placeholder)\n- `labels`: `string[]` — Labels to add\n\n**Example:**\n```json\n{\"op\": \"label_add\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"labels\": [\"urgent\", \"backend\"]}\n```\n\n##### 7. Remove Labels (`label_remove`)\n\nRemoves labels from a bead.\n\n**Required fields:**\n- `op`: `\"label_remove\"`\n- `id`: `string` — Bead ID (can use placeholder)\n- `labels`: `string[]` — Labels to remove\n\n**Example:**\n```json\n{\"op\": \"label_remove\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"labels\": [\"deprecated\"]}\n```\n\n##### 8. Add Comment (`comment`)\n\nAdds a comment to a bead.\n\n**Required fields:**\n- `op`: `\"comment\"`\n- `id`: `string` — Bead ID (can use placeholder)\n- `text`: `string` — Comment text\n\n**Optional fields:**\n- `author`: `string` — Comment author (default: `\"batch\"`)\n\n**Example:**\n```json\n{\"op\": \"comment\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"text\": \"Found edge case in login flow\", \"author\": \"worker-7\"}\n```\n\n#### Batch Execution Examples\n\n**NEEDLE mitosis: split 1 bead into N children atomically**\n\nMethod 1: Dedicated mitosis command (recommended)\n```bash\nbf mitosis bf-a3f8 \\\n  --children '[\n    {\"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2},\n    {\"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\", \"priority\": 2}\n  ]' \\\n  --reason \"Split into children\"\n```\n\nMethod 2: Direct batch with placeholder references\n```bash\nbf batch --json '[\n  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Implement login handler\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"Add session tests\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"blocker\": \"@0\"},\n  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"blocker\": \"@1\"},\n  {\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"bf-a3f8\", \"reason\": \"Split into children\"}\n]'\n```\n\n**Bulk status update:**\n```bash\nbf batch --json '[\n  {\"op\": \"update\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"status\": \"in_progress\"},\n  {\"op\": \"update\", \"id\": \"bf-456\", \"status\": \"in_progress\"},\n  {\"op\": \"comment\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"text\": \"Started work\"}\n]'\n```\n\n**Label management:**\n```bash\nbf batch --json '[\n  {\"op\": \"label_add\", \"id\": \"bf-123\", \"labels\": [\"urgent\", \"backend\"]},\n  {\"op\": \"label_remove\", \"id\": \"bf-456\", \"labels\": [\"deprecated\"]}\n]'\n```\n\n#### Batch Response Format\n\nReturns a JSON array of results, one per operation:\n\n```json\n[\n  {\"op\": 0, \"status\": \"ok\", \"id\": \"bf-new1\", \"message\": \"Created bead bf-new1\"},\n  {\"op\": 1, \"status\": \"ok\", \"id\": \"bf-new2\", \"message\": \"Created bead bf-new2\"},\n  {\"op\": 2, \"status\": \"ok\", \"message\": \"ok: bf-parent blocked by bf-new1\"},\n  {\"op\": 3, \"status\": \"ok\", \"message\": \"Closed bead bf-parent\"}\n]\n```\n\nOn error, the transaction rolls back and no partial state is committed:\n\n```json\n[\n  {\"op\": 0, \"status\": \"ok\", \"id\": \"bf-new1\", \"message\": \"Created bead bf-new1\"},\n  {\"op\": 1, \"status\": \"error\", \"error\": \"Bead not found: bf-missing\", \"message\": null}\n]\n```\n\n#### Field Validation\n\nUnknown fields in any operation are rejected with a clear error message listing allowed fields. This catches typos early:\n\n```bash\nbf batch --json '[{\"op\": \"create\", \"titlle\": \" typo\"}]'\n# Error: Unknown field 'titlle' in operation 'create'. Allowed fields: op, title, type, priority, description, assignee, labels\n```\n\n### Extensible Annotations\n\nArbitrary key-value metadata on any bead, transparent to `br`:\n\n```bash\nbf annotate set bf-a3f8 needle_attempt 3\nbf annotate set bf-a3f8 needle_session abc123\nbf annotate set bf-a3f8 review_status needs_review\nbf list --annotation needle_attempt=3\n```\n\n### Operation History\n\n```bash\nbf log bf-a3f8\n\n2026-04-29 10:00  CREATED     by: human                  \"Implement auth flow\"\n2026-04-29 14:30  CLAIMED     by: worker-3 (sonnet-4-6)  open → in_progress\n2026-04-29 15:45  COMMENT     by: worker-3               \"Found edge case\"\n2026-04-29 16:00  CLOSED      by: worker-3               \"Completed\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### Secret Scanning (Pre-Commit Hook)\n\n`bf` scans for secrets before writing to the database (see `.beads/config.yaml` → `secret_protection`). The `bf commit-check` command extends this to git — it runs as a pre-commit hook to block commits that would add secrets to `.beads/` files.\n\n```bash\n# Manual scan\nbf commit-check\n# Exits 0 (clean) or 1 (secrets found) with detailed error output\n```\n\n**Installation as git pre-commit hook:**\n\n```bash\n# In your workspace repo\ncat > .git/hooks/pre-commit << 'EOF'\n#!/bin/sh\nbf commit-check\nEOF\n\nchmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit\n```\n\n**What gets scanned:**\n- `.beads/config.yaml` — workspace configuration\n- `.beads/metadata.json` — database path settings\n- `.beads/issues.jsonl` — bead data (git artifact)\n\n**Patterns detected:**\n- AWS keys (`AKIA...`, secret access keys)\n- GitHub tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`)\n- Private keys (`BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`, `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`)\n- JWT tokens\n- API keys in URLs\n- Database connection strings\n- And more (same scanner as write-time protection)\n\n**Allowlist exceptions:**\n\nIf a pattern is legitimately non-secret, add to `.beads/config.yaml`:\n\n```yaml\nsecret_protection:\n  allowlist:\n    - \"^AKIAEXAMPLE$\"  # exact string\n    - \"password: test\"  # substring\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commands\n\nMost commands accept `--format json|text|toon` for output and a global `-w/--workspace <path>` to target a workspace other than the current directory. The global `--no-auto-flush` flag disables the post-mutation incremental JSONL export for that one invocation (mutations stay db-only and marked dirty until `bf sync --flush-only`); see [Auto-Flush](#auto-flush-phase-71--the-checkpoint-tracks-the-live-store) below.\n\n```\n# ── Lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf create        --title \"...\" [--type <t>] [--priority <N>] [--description \"...\"]\n                 [--assignee <a>] [--label <l> ...]\nbf list          [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>]\n                 [--annotation k=v] [--limit <N>] [--all] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\nbf show          <id> [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\nbf update        <id> [--title \"...\"] [--status <s>] [--priority <N>] [--assignee <a>]\n                 [--description \"...\"] [--description-file <path>] [--acceptance-criteria \"...\"]\n                 [--notes \"...\"] [--design \"...\"] [--due-at <RFC3339>]\nbf close         <id> [--reason \"...\"]\nbf reopen        <id>\nbf delete        <id>\nbf ready         [--limit <N>] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]   # unblocked beads\nbf count         [--status <s>]\n\n# ── Claiming & concurrency ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf claim         --assignee <id> [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--harness-version <v>]\n                 [--any] [--fallback <mode>] [--workspace-paths <p> ...] [--dry-run]\n                 [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\nbf batch         [--file ops.json] [--json '[...]'] [--stdin]       # atomic multi-op\nbf mitosis       <id> --children '[...]' [--reason \"...\"] [--format ...]   # split into children\n\n# ── Dependencies & structure ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf dep add       <blocker> --blocks <blocked> [-t <type>]   # blocker must close first\nbf dep remove    <issue> <depends-on>\nbf dep list      <id>\nbf dep tree      <id> [-d down|up|both] [--max-depth <N>] [--format ...] [--json]\nbf critical-path <epic-id> [--max-depth <N>] [--format ...]\n\n# ── Labels, comments, annotations ────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf label add     --label <l> [<l> ...] <id>\nbf label remove  --label <l> [<l> ...] <id>\nbf label list    [<id>]                  # all unique labels if id omitted\nbf labels        <id> [--format text|json]                  # efficient single-bead SELECT\nbf comments add  <id> <text ...>\nbf comments list <id>\nbf annotate set    <id> <key> <value>\nbf annotate get    <id> <key>\nbf annotate remove <id> <key>\nbf annotate list   <id>\nbf annotate clear  <id>\n\n# ── Query & history ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf search        [<query>] [-s <status> ...] [-t <type> ...] [--assignee <a>]\n                 [-l <label> ...] [--priority-min <N>] [--priority-max <N>] [--limit <N>]\n                 [--format json|text|toon]\nbf recent        [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>]\n                 [--since <RFC3339>] [--before <RFC3339>] [-t <period>] [-n <N>]\n                 [--format json|text|toon] [--json]           # period: e.g. 1h, 24h, 7d, 4w\nbf log           [<id>] [--limit <N>] [--since <RFC3339>] [--actor <a>]\n                 [--status-changes] [--diff] [--git] [--format json|text|toon] [--json]\nbf stats         [--by-type] [--by-priority] [--by-assignee] [--by-label] [--format ...]\nbf velocity      [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--format json|text|toon]\n\n# ── Maintenance & config ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nbf sync          [--flush-only] [--import-only]\nbf merge-jsonl   --ours <A> --theirs <B> [--base <O>] [--output <path>]  # 3-way JSONL merge / git driver\nbf doctor        [--repair [--flush-first] [--force]] [--reclaim-stale [--ttl <minutes>]]  # no flags = health check\nbf rotate        [--days <N>] [--dry-run]\nbf migrate       [--workspace <p>] [--from-jsonl] [--seed-velocity] [--dry-run] [--skip-verify]\nbf init          [--prefix <p>]\nbf schema        [<target|id>] [--format json|text]      # \"all\" = DDL; a bead id = full JSON\nbf config        list | get <key> | set <key> <value> | path\nbf commit-check  # git pre-commit hook for secret scanning\n```\n\nAll `br` commands work identically. `bf` is a strict superset.\n\n---\n\n## Output Formats\n\nMost read commands accept `--format text|json|toon` (or the `--json` alias for\n`--format json`). The JSON shape depends on **which command** you run, and it is\nnot always a JSON array.\n\n### Listing commands emit JSONL — not a JSON array\n\n`bf list`, `bf ready`, `bf search`, and `bf recent` with `--format json` emit\n**JSONL**: one self-contained, compact JSON object per line, joined by newlines,\nwith **no array wrapper** and no commas between objects.\n\n```bash\n$ bf list --format json\n{\"id\":\"test-3qv\",\"title\":\"alpha task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,\"issue_type\":\"task\",\"assignee\":null,\"labels\":[],\"created_at\":\"2026-07-22T15:54:16Z\",...}\n{\"id\":\"test-2c4\",\"title\":\"beta task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,\"issue_type\":\"task\",\"assignee\":null,\"labels\":[],\"created_at\":\"2026-07-22T15:54:16Z\",...}\n```\n\nThe concatenated stdout is **not** valid JSON (`{\"a\":1}\\n{\"b\":2}` is two values,\nnot one), so you cannot `json.loads()` the whole buffer. Parse it **line by\nline**:\n\n```python\nimport json, subprocess\nout = subprocess.check_output([\"bf\", \"list\", \"--format\", \"json\"], text=True)\nbeads = [json.loads(line) for line in out.splitlines() if line.strip()]\n```\n\n```bash\n# jq: slurp the JSONL lines into one array, then operate on it\nbf list --format json | jq -s 'map(.id)'\n```\n\nTwo keys are **always** present on every emitted object, even on a bare bead:\n\n- `assignee` — `null` when unassigned (never omitted)\n- `labels` — an array, `[]` when empty (never omitted)\n\nThe on-disk `issues.jsonl` checkpoint (written by `bf sync`) omits these when\nunset to stay compact; the CLI `--format json` path normalizes them back so a\ndownstream struct with non-optional `assignee`/`labels` fields deserializes\ncleanly.\n\n**Empty results differ by command:**\n\n| Command | Empty `--format json` output |\n|---------|------------------------------|\n| `bf list` | nothing (empty stdout) |\n| `bf search` / `bf recent` | nothing (empty stdout) |\n| `bf ready` | `[]` |\n\n`ready` is the one listing command that special-cases emptiness to `[]`; the\nothers print nothing at all.\n\n### `bf show` emits a one-element array\n\nUnlike the listing commands, `bf show <id> --format json` wraps the single bead\nin a **JSON array of one element**:\n\n```bash\n$ bf show test-3qv --format json\n[{\"id\":\"test-3qv\",\"title\":\"alpha task\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":2,...}]\n```\n\nThis is deliberate: NEEDLE's `parse_single_bead` expects `Vec<Bead>` and takes\nthe first element, so `show` ships an array to stay parse-compatible with that\ncode path.\n\n### `bf claim` emits a single object\n\n`bf claim --json` prints one JSON object describing the claim (or `{}` when\nnothing was claimed) — never an array, never an `Issue`:\n\n```bash\n$ bf claim --assignee worker-7 --json\n{\"bead_id\":\"test-3qv\",\"assignee\":\"worker-7\",\"reclaimed\":0}\n```\n\n`bf velocity --format json` emits a JSON array of stat objects (`[]` when empty).\n\n### `br` produces byte-identical output\n\n`br` delegates to the `bf` binary — either directly (a symlink, as installed by\n`ln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br`) or via a logging shim that writes a\ndeprecation-telemetry line and then `exec bf \"$@\"`. Neither path touches stdout,\nso every `br` command emits **byte-identical** output to its `bf` equivalent —\nsame JSONL, same array wrapping for `show`, same empty-case behavior. A parser\nwritten for `br list --format json` works unchanged for `bf list --format json`,\nand vice versa.\n\n---\n\n## NEEDLE Integration\n\nReplace the five non-atomic `br` chains in `bead_store/mod.rs`:\n\n| Old (racy) | New (atomic) |\n|-----------|--------------|\n| `br ready` → `br update` → `br show` (3 calls, 2 race windows) | `bf claim` (1 call, 1 transaction) |\n| `br create` + `br dep add` (orphan if crash between) | `bf batch` (crash-safe, all-or-nothing) |\n| `br show` just to get `.labels` field | `bf labels <id>` (direct `SELECT` on labels table) |\n| N × `br label add` loops (N processes) | `bf label <id> add l1 l2 l3` (one transaction) |\n\nBackward compatibility — install `br` as a symlink:\n\n```bash\nln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n```\n\n---\n\n## Compatibility\n\n`bf` reads and writes the same SQLite schema and JSONL format as `br`. A workspace used by `bf` can be read by `br` and vice versa. Verified by three test suites (see plan §Compatibility Verification):\n\n1. **JSONL round-trip**: `br list --format json` == `bf list --format json` on the same workspace\n2. **SQLite compat**: `bf` writes, `br` reads, `br doctor` passes\n3. **Claim race**: 20 concurrent `bf claim` processes, 10 beads — exactly 10 claims succeed, no bead claimed twice\n\n---\n\n## Reliability\n\n- **rusqlite** (standard SQLite C library) — not FrankenSQLite, which had known corruption under concurrent writes\n- **WAL mode** — concurrent reads never block writes; writers queue, not corrupt\n- **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — acquires write lock before any reads; eliminates TOCTOU\n- **`SQLITE_BUSY` retry** — exponential backoff up to 5 retries; converts contention spikes to short waits\n\n### Data Authority Model\n\n**bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br**:\n\n| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n|------|----------------|-----------------|\n| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n\nThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. All mutations (create/update/claim) go to SQLite. With `sync.auto_flush` (default **on**), every successful mutation also incrementally exports the changed beads to `issues.jsonl`, so the checkpoint tracks the live store instead of trailing it — a separate flush is no longer needed in normal operation.\n\n### Auto-Flush (Phase 7.1) — the checkpoint tracks the live store\n\nWith `sync.auto_flush` (default **on**), every successful mutation (`create`/`update`/`claim`/`close`/`batch`) incrementally exports just the changed beads to `issues.jsonl` (a surgical line replacement, not a full rewrite). The JSONL artifact therefore stays current with SQLite after every command — no separate flush step is required in normal operation. Read-only and diagnostic commands never write the JSONL.\n\n```yaml\n# .beads/config.yaml\nsync:\n  auto_flush: true     # default; set false to make mutations db-only until bf sync --flush-only\n```\n\n```bash\nbf create --title \"...\"               # auto-flushed by default → already in issues.jsonl\nbf create --title \"...\" --no-auto-flush   # per-invocation override: db-only, marked dirty\n```\n\n**Flush failure never fails the mutation.** Auto-flush is best-effort: if the incremental export fails, the mutation still commits, the dirty mark is retained, and the failure is surfaced loudly — a `warning:` line on stderr and a non-null `warning` field in the `--json` envelope naming the recovery command. The dirty bead stays recoverable.\n\n**Named recovery.** `bf sync --flush-only` is the explicit checkpoint and the recovery path: it clears the entire `dirty_issues` set and rewrites a **full** checkpoint (every bead, not just the dirty one). Run it after an auto-flush warning, or to produce a clean git-committable snapshot:\n\n```bash\nbf sync --flush-only\n```\n\n### Repair safety — protection is in the doctor, not a manual ritual\n\n`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from `issues.jsonl`. Because auto-flush keeps the checkpoint current, the old \"ALWAYS `bf sync --flush-only` before repair\" ritual (added after the 2026-06-10 incident where seven agents across seven workspaces each lost their first batch of fresh beads to a post-create `doctor --repair`; four db-only beads in ARMOR — bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44 — were permanently lost) is **obsolete**. The data-loss guard now lives in the doctor command itself: it **refuses** to repair when unflushed (db-only) beads exist, and tells you exactly what to do.\n\n```bash\nbf doctor                              # health check — reports \"Unflushed beads: N\" if any\nbf doctor --repair                     # REFUSES if unflushed beads exist (no data loss)\nbf doctor --repair --flush-first       # checkpoint unflushed beads first, then rebuild\nbf doctor --repair --force             # proceed anyway — unflushed beads WILL be lost\n```\n\nKilling a worker at any point between mutation and flush loses nothing that `git diff .beads/` can't show: with auto-flush on the bead is already in the artifact when the command returns; with auto-flush off the bead survives in SQLite (marked dirty) and is recovered by `bf sync --flush-only`. Pinned by `tests/recovery_and_exit_criteria.rs`.\n\n### Multi-Box & Fleet Hardening (Phase 7.9)\n\nWhen the same repo is checked out on several boxes, each keeps its own live `beads.db` and shares state through the git-committed `issues.jsonl`. Three layers defend that shared artifact:\n\n**Three-way JSONL merge** — a plain git text merge of `issues.jsonl` is unsafe: each line is a whole bead, so a textual conflict marker corrupts JSON and \"take theirs\" silently drops beads. `bf merge-jsonl` merges **per-bead** against a common ancestor instead. Resolution is deterministic: a one-sided edit is taken as-is; a two-sided edit resolves last-writer-wins by `updated_at` (ties broken by content hash, so the result is independent of which box runs the merge); a delete that races a concurrent edit keeps the edit (never silently discards work). Wire it as a git merge driver:\n\n```bash\ngit config merge.beads.name   \"bead-forge 3-way JSONL merge\"\ngit config merge.beads.driver \"bf merge-jsonl --base %O --ours %A --theirs %B --output %A\"\necho '.beads/issues.jsonl merge=beads' >> .gitattributes\n```\n\n**Merge anchor** (`.beads/beads.base.jsonl`) — every full flush/import refreshes this snapshot of the last state this box agreed on with the artifact. It is the fallback three-way base for `bf merge-jsonl` when git does not supply `%O` (out-of-band merges across checkouts). Local-only; git-ignored.\n\n**Pre-export history backups** (`.beads/.bf_history/`) — before every full flush overwrites `issues.jsonl`, the previous version is copied into `.bf_history/` and pruned to the newest `history.max_backups` snapshots (default 20). One more recovery layer under a bad export or merge. Enabled by default; disable with `history.enabled: false` in `config.yaml`. Local-only; git-ignored.\n\n**Fleet concurrency tests** (`tests/fleet_concurrency.rs`) — spawn N concurrent `bf` *processes* doing create/claim/close and assert the upstream bug classes stay dead: no parallel-write silent loss (`count` equals successful creates), no loss across flush + fresh-DB reimport, and no bead claimed twice under a 20-worker herd on 15 beads.\n\n---\n\n## Implementation\n\nSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](plan/plan.md) for the complete implementation plan including:\n\n- Exact SQLite schema (all 13 tables + indexes)\n- `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` retry wrapper implementation\n- Critical path CTE algorithm\n- Velocity stats schema and claim scoring formula\n- Compatibility verification test suites\n- NEEDLE integration specifics (file, line numbers, before/after)\n\n---\n\n## Migration from br to bf\n\n### Output Format Compatibility (no parser changes)\n\nMigrating to `bf` requires **no changes to JSON consumers**. `bf` is a drop-in\nreplacement: every command emits byte-identical output to `br`, because `br`\ndelegates to the `bf` binary (via symlink, or a logging shim that `exec bf\n\"$@\"`) and never alters stdout.\n\nThe format to keep in mind (full details in [§ Output Formats](#output-formats)):\n\n- `list` / `ready` / `search` / `recent --format json` → **JSONL** (one object\n  per line, not a JSON array). Parse line-by-line — do not `json.loads()` the\n  whole buffer.\n- `show <id> --format json` → a **one-element array** (for NEEDLE's\n  `parse_single_bead`).\n- Empty `list`/`search`/`recent` print nothing; empty `ready` prints `[]`.\n\nAny script that already parses `br list --format json` line-by-line keeps\nworking unchanged against `bf`.\n\n### Per-Machine Installation\n\n```bash\n# Install bf binary\ncurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\n  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n\n# Drop-in replace br (all existing scripts work unchanged)\nln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n\n# Verify installation\nbf --version\nbr --version  # should show same version\n```\n\n### Per-Workspace Migration\n\n**Standard migration** (Path B: explicit, with backup and verification):\n\n```bash\n# Migrate a single workspace\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace\n\n# Or migrate all workspaces in a loop\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  bf migrate --workspace \"$workspace\"\ndone\n```\n\n**What `bf migrate` does:**\n1. Acquires migration lock (prevents concurrent claims during migration)\n2. Backs up `beads.db` → `beads.db.br-backup-<timestamp>`\n3. Applies schema migrations (creates bf-only tables via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`)\n4. Primes critical_path_cache for all epics\n5. Seeds `config.yaml` with bf-specific defaults if missing\n6. Verifies forward compatibility (br can still open the database)\n7. Verifies backward compatibility (`bf doctor` health check passes)\n8. Releases migration lock\n\n**Dry-run mode** (see what would happen without making changes):\n\n```bash\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace --dry-run\n```\n\n**Recovery mode** (for corrupted/missing databases):\n\nIf `beads.db` is corrupted or missing, `bf migrate --from-jsonl` rebuilds from `issues.jsonl` and reconstructs events from git history:\n\n```bash\nbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace --from-jsonl [--seed-velocity]\n```\n\n### Migration Checklist\n\n**Step 1: Per-machine installation**\n\n```bash\n# Install bf binary\ncurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\n  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n\n# Drop-in replace br (all existing scripts work unchanged)\nln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n\n# Verify installation\nbf --version\nbr --version  # should show same version\n```\n\n**Step 2: Per-workspace migration loop**\n\n```bash\n# Migrate all workspaces\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  echo \"Migrating $workspace...\"\n  bf migrate --workspace \"$workspace\"\ndone\n```\n\n**Step 3: Verify each migration**\n\n```bash\n# Verify each workspace passes both doctor checks\nfor workspace in \\\n  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n  echo \"Checking $workspace...\"\n  cd \"$workspace\" || continue\n  echo \"  bf doctor:\"\n  bf doctor || echo \"  ❌ bf doctor failed\"\n  echo \"  br doctor:\"\n  br doctor || echo \"  ❌ br doctor failed\"\ndone\n```\n\nBoth `bf doctor` and `br doctor` should exit 0 with no errors for each workspace.\n\n**Step 4: Update NEEDLE adapter configs**\n\nAfter migration, update NEEDLE adapter configs to pass worker metadata for velocity tracking:\n\n```yaml\n# In .config/needle/adapters/claude-sonnet.yaml, update invoke_template:\nbf claim --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --harness-version 0.5.2 ...\n```\n\nThis enables velocity-aware routing (see §Velocity-Aware Scoring above).\n\n### Verification After Migration\n\nFor each workspace, verify both tools can read the database:\n\n```bash\n# Verify bf doctor passes (no flags = health check)\ncd /path/to/workspace\nbf doctor\n\n# Verify br doctor passes (forward compatibility)\nbr doctor\n```\n\nBoth commands should exit 0 with no errors.\n\n**Known limitation:** The migration may show a forward compatibility warning: \"Forward compatibility check failed: issues table column count mismatch\". skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub deleted_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub deleted_by: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub delete_reason: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub original_type: Option<String>,\n\n    // Compaction (legacy/compat)\n    // Note: Always serialize compaction_level as integer (0 when None) for bd conformance\n    // bd's Go sql scanner cannot handle NULL for integer columns\n    #[serde(default, serialize_with = \"serialize_compaction_level\")]\n    pub compaction_level: Option<i32>,\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub compacted_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub compacted_at_commit: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub original_size: Option<i32>,\n\n    // Messaging\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub sender: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"is_false\")]\n    pub ephemeral: bool,\n\n    // Context\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"is_false\")]\n    pub pinned: bool,\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"is_false\")]\n    pub is_template: bool,\n\n    // Relations (for export/display, not always in DB table directly)\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Vec::is_empty\", default)]\n    pub labels: Vec<String>,\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Vec::is_empty\", default)]\n    pub dependencies: Vec<Dependency>,\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Vec::is_empty\", default)]\n    pub comments: Vec<Comment>,\n\n    // Annotations (bf-only: arbitrary key-value metadata stored in bead_annotations table)\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"BTreeMap::is_empty\")]\n    pub annotations: BTreeMap<String, String>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Issue {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            id: String::new(),\n            content_hash: None,\n            title: String::new(),\n            description: None,\n            design: None,\n            acceptance_criteria: None,\n            notes: None,\n            status: Status::default(),\n            priority: Priority::default(),\n            issue_type: IssueType::default(),\n            assignee: None,\n            owner: None,\n            estimated_minutes: None,\n            created_at: Utc::now(),\n            created_by: None,\n            updated_at: Utc::now(),\n            closed_at: None,\n            close_reason: None,\n            closed_by_session: None,\n            due_at: None,\n            defer_until: None,\n            external_ref: None,\n            source_system: None,\n            source_repo: None,\n            deleted_at: None,\n            deleted_by: None,\n            delete_reason: None,\n            original_type: None,\n            compaction_level: None,\n            compacted_at: None,\n            compacted_at_commit: None,\n            original_size: None,\n            sender: None,\n            ephemeral: false,\n            pinned: false,\n            is_template: false,\n            labels: Vec::new(),\n            dependencies: Vec::new(),\n            comments: Vec::new(),\n            annotations: BTreeMap::new(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Issue {\n    pub fn new(id: String, title: String, source_repo: String) -> Self {\n        let now = Utc::now();\n        Issue {\n            id,\n            title,\n            source_repo: Some(source_repo),\n            created_at: now,\n            updated_at: now,\n            status: Status::default(),\n            priority: Priority::default(),\n            issue_type: IssueType::default(),\n            ..Default::default()\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_blocked(&self) -> bool {\n        self.dependencies\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|d| matches!(d.dep_type, DependencyType::Blocks))\n            .any(|d| {\n                self.source_repo\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|repo| repo == &d.depends_on_id)\n                    .unwrap_or(false)\n            })\n    }\n\n    pub fn content_hash(&self) -> String {\n        use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};\n        let serialized = serde_json::to_string(self).unwrap_or_default();\n        let hash = Sha256::digest(serialized.as_bytes());\n        format!(\"{:x}\", hash)\n    }\n\n    /// Compare two issues using sync semantics instead of raw struct equality.\n    ///\n    /// This ignores derived or volatile audit fields that would otherwise make\n    /// semantically identical issues look different across import/export\n    /// boundaries, while still comparing the full synced payload including\n    /// labels, dependencies, comments, and user-visible timestamps like `due_at`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn sync_equals(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {\n        if self.id != other.id\n            || self.title != other.title\n            || self.description != other.description\n            || self.design != other.design\n            || self.acceptance_criteria != other.acceptance_criteria\n            || self.notes != other.notes\n            || self.status != other.status\n            || self.priority != other.priority\n            || self.issue_type != other.issue_type\n            || self.assignee != other.assignee\n            || self.owner != other.owner\n            || self.estimated_minutes != other.estimated_minutes\n            || self.created_by != other.created_by\n            || self.closed_at != other.closed_at\n            || self.close_reason != other.close_reason\n            || self.closed_by_session != other.closed_by_session\n            || self.due_at != other.due_at\n            || self.defer_until != other.defer_until\n            || self.external_ref != other.external_ref\n            || self.source_system != other.source_system\n            || self.source_repo != other.source_repo\n            || self.deleted_at != other.deleted_at\n            || self.deleted_by != other.deleted_by\n            || self.delete_reason != other.delete_reason\n            || self.original_type != other.original_type\n            || self.compacted_at != other.compacted_at\n            || self.compacted_at_commit != other.compacted_at_commit\n            || self.original_size != other.original_size\n            || self.sender != other.sender\n            || self.ephemeral != other.ephemeral\n            || self.pinned != other.pinned\n            || self.is_template != other.is_template\n        {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Handle compaction_level serialization quirk where None == 0\n        if self.compaction_level.unwrap_or(0) != other.compaction_level.unwrap_or(0) {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Fast path for relations: if lengths differ, they can't be equal\n        if self.dependencies.len() != other.dependencies.len()\n            || self.comments.len() != other.comments.len()\n        {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Compare labels (order independent)\n        let mut self_labels = self.labels.clone();\n        self_labels.sort_unstable();\n        self_labels.dedup();\n        let mut other_labels = other.labels.clone();\n        other_labels.sort_unstable();\n        other_labels.dedup();\n        if self_labels != other_labels {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Compare dependencies (order independent)\n        let mut self_deps = self.dependencies.clone();\n        self_deps.sort_by(|left, right| {\n            left.issue_id\n                .cmp(&right.issue_id)\n                .then_with(|| left.depends_on_id.cmp(&right.depends_on_id))\n                .then_with(|| left.dep_type.as_str().cmp(right.dep_type.as_str()))\n                .then_with(|| left.created_at.cmp(&right.created_at))\n                .then_with(|| left.created_by.cmp(&right.created_by))\n                .then_with(|| left.metadata.cmp(&right.metadata))\n                .then_with(|| left.thread_id.cmp(&right.thread_id))\n        });\n        let mut other_deps = other.dependencies.clone();\n        other_deps.sort_by(|left, right| {\n            left.issue_id\n                .cmp(&right.issue_id)\n                .then_with(|| left.depends_on_id.cmp(&right.depends_on_id))\n                .then_with(|| left.dep_type.as_str().cmp(right.dep_type.as_str()))\n                .then_with(|| left.created_at.cmp(&right.created_at))\n                .then_with(|| left.created_by.cmp(&right.created_by))\n                .then_with(|| left.metadata.cmp(&right.metadata))\n                .then_with(|| left.thread_id.cmp(&right.thread_id))\n        });\n        if self_deps != other_deps {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Compare comments (order independent)\n        let mut self_comments = self.comments.clone();\n        self_comments.sort_by(|left, right| {\n            left.issue_id\n                .cmp(&right.issue_id)\n                .then_with(|| left.created_at.cmp(&right.created_at))\n                .then_with(|| left.author.cmp(&right.author))\n                .then_with(|| left.body.cmp(&right.body))\n                .then_with(|| left.id.cmp(&right.id))\n        });\n        let mut other_comments = other.comments.clone();\n        other_comments.sort_by(|left, right| {\n            left.issue_id\n                .cmp(&right.issue_id)\n                .then_with(|| left.created_at.cmp(&right.created_at))\n                .then_with(|| left.author.cmp(&right.author))\n                .then_with(|| left.body.cmp(&right.body))\n                .then_with(|| left.id.cmp(&right.id))\n        });\n        if self_comments != other_comments {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// Check if this issue is a tombstone that has exceeded its TTL.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_expired_tombstone(&self, retention_days: Option<u64>) -> bool {\n        if self.status != Status::Tombstone {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        let Some(days) = retention_days else {\n            return false;\n        };\n\n        if days == 0 {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        let Some(deleted_at) = self.deleted_at else {\n            return false;\n        };\n\n        // Clamp days to a safe maximum to avoid panic in Duration::days().\n        let max_safe_days = 365_u64 * 1000;\n        let days_i64 = i64::try_from(days.min(max_safe_days)).unwrap_or(365_000);\n        let expiration_time = deleted_at + chrono::Duration::days(days_i64);\n        Utc::now() > expiration_time\n    }\n}\n\n/// Epic completion status with child counts.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct EpicStatus {\n    pub epic: Issue,\n    pub total_children: usize,\n    pub closed_children: usize,\n    pub eligible_for_close: bool,\n}\n\n/// Relationship between two issues.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Dependency {\n    ///    /// Thread ID for conversation linking.\n    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub thread_id: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Dependency {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            issue_id: String::new(),\n            depends_on_id: String::new(),\n            dep_type: DependencyType::Blocks,\n            created_at: Utc::now(),\n            created_by: None,\n            metadata: None,\n            thread_id: None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A comment on an issue.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub
